build.note: Re-analysis of the 14 and 15 October single-shot pair recordings (L4040, L4042, L4043); no new capture, game not launched.

question: Which of the candidate mechanisms for the recovery tail (two-pool recovery, a camera spring between the recoil state and the view, a recovery clock not reset by the second shot) does the camera track of the pair videos show, and does the camera at shot 2 agree with the bullet-hole pair separations?

sourceFacts.method: camera-track-pairs.py: the burst camera-track method of L4045 applied to every pair in the AK-205 (6 bands), LMR27 (3 bands, two days) and TR-7 (5 bands) clips, both suppressors; the 1x layer left of the scope registered to a fixed reference frame before shot 1 (direct track) and to the previous frame (chain cross-check) by gradient cross-correlation with a sub-pixel peak; kick onsets found on the track near the HUD counter frames; curve A pooled after shot 1 per weapon and load, curve B per band after shot 2; predict-pairs.mjs gives the simulator mean trace at 1 ms under the stored law, the x0.8 law, the two-pool variant of L4044 and a no-reset variant; cross-check against pairs6-summary.json of each run. See ANALYSIS.md.

control.description: 356 of 377 pairs pass the quality check (onsets at the HUD gap within 2 frames, correlation to the reference at least 0.3, chain within 0.1 deg of the direct track); the pre-shot baseline is flat to 0.003 deg; the camera at shot 2 reproduces the hole separation on the AK-205 133 ms bands (+0.015 / +0.041) and reaches zero or slightly below on every band from 430 ms, where the hole values are the two-star fit floor.

points: Ringing after every kick: peak on frame 4 after the onset (5 to 7 on the LMR27), a dip 2 to 3 frames later, a second maximum on frame 14 (117 ms) on all six weapon-load combinations; settled after 8 (AK-205), 6 (LMR27) and 10 (TR-7) frames, not ordered by kick size; dip depth 0.22 / 0.41 deg on the AK-205 / TR-7 (0.44 / 0.35 of the kick), 0.09 on the LMR27, halved by the Lightened Suppressor's 50 ms delivery.

Return after a single shot against the x0.8 law: AK-205 +0.12 deg from 200 to 300 ms (0.23 of the kick), zero at 408 ms (law 289); TR-7 +0.25 to +0.33 from 200 to 330 ms (0.23 to 0.29 of the kick), zero at 458 / 433 ms (law 374 / 347) with an undershoot of -0.04 / -0.05; LMR27 within 0.06 to 300 ms and +0.05 to +0.07 from 330 to 500 ms, zero at 625 ms (Lightened; law 493). The law with its time axis stretched by x1.35 / x1.40 (AK-205), x1.35 / x1.40 (TR-7) and x1.10 / x1.05 (LMR27) fits the camera from 167 to 400 ms to an rms of 0.002 / 0.005, 0.024 / 0.036 and 0.036 / 0.034 deg (plain law 0.096, 0.233, 0.052).

Descent rate from 200 to 330 ms: 1.3 to 1.8 deg/s on the AK-205 and 3.2 to 3.9 deg/s on the TR-7, near-constant while the displacement falls by a factor 2.5 to 3, where the law decelerates from the same rate to zero; the same signature as the 28 to 31 deg/s descent after the 15-round bursts (L4045), scaled to the starting displacement, so not a fixed rate cap.

Clock test: the return after shot 2 minus the return after shot 1 at the same elapsed time matches the reset law within 0.03 deg (AK-205), 0.04 (LMR27) and 0.1 (TR-7) on all 36 bands; the no-reset variant is 0.1 to 0.6 deg off at 100 to 267 ms after shot 2.

Camera at shot 2 minus the hole separation: AK-205 +0.041 / +0.015 at 133 ms, +0.080 / +0.104 at 167, +0.065 / +0.075 at 233, +0.029 / +0.048 at 292 to 296, -0.009 / -0.021 at 333 ms; LMR27 +0.098 / +0.122 at 233 ms (15 Oct), +0.077 / +0.022 at 342 to 350 ms (14 Oct +0.096 / -0.003); TR-7 +0.292 / +0.362 at 267 ms, +0.137 / +0.126 at 350 ms (Standard / Lightened, degrees; standard errors 0.017 to 0.04). From 430 ms the camera is at -0.03 to +0.01 on every band. The camera shows the Lightened Suppressor advantage on the LMR27 at 300 to 400 ms (0.06 to 0.07 deg, law 0.05 to 0.06) that the holes lack.

inference: The recovery clock is reset by every shot, as the site law assumes. The pair tail at 290 to 350 ms is real in the camera, and on the AK-205 and the LMR27 Lightened the camera and the holes agree there, so the tail is in the aim the bullets follow; it is the end of a descent that runs at a near-constant rate instead of decelerating, which is the same thing the 15-round bursts showed at 30 deg/s, scaled to the displacement. A two-pool recovery in its fitted form (10% of the kick at 2/s) does not match: the camera excess over the law is 2 to 5 times larger at 230 to 330 ms, is not a fixed fraction of the kick across weapons (0.23 to 0.29 on the AK-205 and TR-7, 0.06 to 0.08 on the LMR27), has no bend and vanishes with an undershoot by 400 to 460 ms. A camera layer between the recoil state and the view exists: every kick rings with a fixed period for 7 to 10 frames, and from 167 to 350 ms the camera sits 4 to 8 standard errors above the holes on the AK-205, LMR27 Standard and TR-7 by an amount that grows with the kick and fades by 330 to 430 ms, so the bullets do not follow the camera in full. The pair data cannot separate a stretched aim plus a small camera offset from a law aim plus a large camera offset on the TR-7; the AK-205 tail and the LMR27 Lightened tail are the places where the two coincide.
unresolved: What the slow kick-proportional camera offset is (a second mode of the camera spring, or the aim itself with the holes under-reading); the LMR27 Standard holes at 333 to 433 ms, which sit 0.07 to 0.10 below the camera while the Lightened holes sit on it; the 0.03 to 0.05 deg undershoot after the return on the TR-7.
siteImpact: None applied; the x0.8 scale and the per-shot clock reset stand. A time-stretched recovery (x1.35 to 1.40 on the 48 / 0.905 and 104 / 1.459 profiles, x1.05 to 1.10 on 13.7 / 0.556) would describe the camera but is not shown to be the aim the bullets follow; no change is proposed from this lead.

leads.title: Camera track of the single-shot pair videos: the recovery clock resets per shot, the camera rings for 7 to 10 frames after every kick and then follows the x0.8 law stretched in time (x1.35 to 1.40 on the AK-205 and TR-7, x1.05 to 1.10 on the LMR27), sitting above the hole separations by a kick-proportional amount that fades by 350 ms
leads.summary: 356 of 377 pairs tracked at 120 fps. The return after shot 2 equals the return after shot 1 plus the residual it started from (no-reset excluded on all 36 bands). After a single shot the camera is above the x0.8 law by +0.12 (AK-205) and +0.25 to +0.33 deg (TR-7) from 200 to 330 ms, within 0.06 on the LMR27, and reaches zero at 408 to 458 ms with a 0.04 undershoot on the TR-7; a two-pool slow pool does not fit (no bend, not a fixed fraction, vanishes by 450 ms). At shot 2 the camera is 0.07 to 0.36 deg above the holes at 167 to 300 ms (4 to 8 standard errors, growing with the kick) and equals them at 333 to 350 ms on the AK-205 and LMR27 Lightened. Descent rate 1.3 to 1.8 deg/s (AK-205) and 3.2 to 3.9 (TR-7), near-constant, the burst signature scaled down.
leads.reopenWhen: A capture that places the bullets against the camera on one shot (impact position per shot on a wall with a reference grid), or a readable implementation of the recovery and camera layers.
